Al Jazeera | datePublished: 2026-10-23T14:56:05Z | dateModified: 2026-10-23T14:56:05Z

Brazil heads into a tense presidential run-off on Sunday 25 October 2026 between incumbent Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and right-wing Senator Flávio Bolsonaro. In the first round on 4 October, Bolsonaro won 47% of the vote to Lula's just over 45%, with the remainder split among smaller conservative candidates — Bolsonaro outperformed expectations, having been expected to trail Lula into the run-off.

The vote will decide whether Brazil joins a growing list of Latin American countries that have elected far-right leaders promising closer ties with the United States; Brazil under Lula has been a key regional holdout against that trend, and a Bolsonaro win would embolden conservatives seeking to extend that streak to the continent's largest economy.

NOTE: This is PREVIEW coverage — the actual run-off vote is Sunday 25 October, so there is no result yet. Flag for the Sunday edition rather than treating as a result today.
